title: Hamas Confirms Death of Izz al-Din al-Haddad, Gaza Armed Wing Commander, Killed in May 15 IDF Rimal Strike
detail: A Hamas official confirmed on May 16, 2026 that Izz al-Din al-Haddad, commander of Hamas's armed wing in Gaza, was killed in the Israeli airstrike on the Rimal neighborhood of Gaza City the previous day. An Israeli official stated al-Haddad had been 'actively undermining Trump's Gaza plan' by organizing continued militant operations during the October 2025 ceasefire. Al-Haddad's elimination is the most senior Hamas military killing since the October 2025 ceasefire began. Hamas vowed to continue resistance operations. The confirmation deepened the Hamas disarmament negotiation deadlock: Hamas has now lost multiple senior commanders since the ceasefire began, and officials have stated that the killings only 'strengthen their resolve.' The cumulative Palestinian death toll under the October 2025 ceasefire now stands at approximately 900+, with disarmament talks at an impasse. Israel maintains it will continue targeted operations until Hamas's military capacity is destroyed.

media.caption: Hamas confirms death of armed wing chief al-Haddad, killed in May 15 IDF airstrike on Rimal, Gaza City — May 16, 2026

title: IDF Strikes Gaza City Residential Building in Rimal; Al Jazeera Films Damage in Wake of Continuing Airstrikes
detail: Israeli forces conducted additional airstrikes on a residential building in the Rimal neighborhood of Gaza City on May 16, 2026. Al Jazeera filmed footage of the aftermath showing extensive structural collapse in the densely populated neighborhood. The strikes continued a pattern of IDF operations in the Rimal area that began with the May 15 strike killing Hamas armed wing chief al-Haddad and at least 6 others and wounding 50+. The Long War Journal reported that Israeli and US officials characterized al-Haddad as a key figure blocking the Trump Gaza plan by coordinating active militant operations during the ceasefire. As of May 16, the cumulative Palestinian death toll since the October 2025 ceasefire exceeded approximately 900. The IDF continued to cite active Hamas ceasefire violations — reporting 19 separate violations between April 21 and May 5 alone — as justification for ongoing strike operations inside Gaza.

title: Tens of Thousands March in London Pro-Palestine Demonstration; 11 Arrested
detail: Tens of thousands of people participated in a pro-Palestine march in London on May 16, 2026, calling for an end to Israeli military operations in Gaza and the West Bank. Police made 11 arrests during the demonstration. The London march occurred concurrently with separate counter-demonstrations. The protest reflected sustained international public opposition to continued Israeli strikes in Gaza despite the October 2025 ceasefire, and came one day after the 78th Nakba anniversary (May 15), which galvanized Palestinian solidarity events across Europe. The London demonstrations are part of a wider pattern of global pro-Palestinian protests that have continued since October 7, 2023, including major demonstrations in the UK, US, France, Germany, and Australia. UK police have faced ongoing debates about protest management and the limits of speech about the conflict.
